# CustomCard

> AI-assisted greeting card maker that scans your calendar and email, drafts a personalized card, and gets it print-ready for any local print shop. Free to create; pay the print shop only if you print.

## What CustomCard does

CustomCard is a personal greeting-card assistant. It:

1. Detects card-worthy occasions by scanning your Google Calendar or Gmail (with permission) — birthdays, weddings, anniversaries, graduations, and more.
2. Asks a short context-aware questionnaire: who the card is from, your relationship to the recipient, tone, any inside details or cultural elements.
3. Drafts personalized copy and artwork directions using AI.
4. Renders a print-ready 5 × 7 folded card (four panels: front, inside-left, inside-right, back) at 300 DPI.
5. Lets you review and edit every word before creating the print package.
6. Prepares downloadable print-ready files for Walgreens, CVS, FedEx Office, or any print shop that accepts PDF or PNG.

No card is auto-sent. No order is placed without explicit user approval.

## Pricing

- **Free to create.** Designing, drafting, and downloading a print package costs nothing.
- **Pay the print shop only when you print.** CustomCard does not handle payment — you confirm the price directly with your chosen print shop (Walgreens, CVS, FedEx Office, etc.).
- **Account optional to start.** You can begin a card without an account. AI generation, saved card history, and Google Calendar connection require a free account.

See /pricing for the full breakdown.

## Key capabilities

- Occasion detection: birthday, graduation, wedding, anniversary, thank-you, sympathy, friendship, belated
- Calendar scanning: Google Calendar integration (optional), manual .ics paste
- Relationship memory: stores approved facts about recipients for future personalization; user can edit or delete any memory
- Multilingual support: non-English messages, right-to-left script
- Cultural sensitivity review: religious phrases, names, cultural details validated before rendering
- 5 × 7 folded card format: four SVG panels at 1500 × 2100 px each, PDF proof
- Vendor-agnostic fulfillment: Walgreens, CVS, FedEx Office, or any print shop accepting standard file formats
- Business/enterprise mode: lifecycle card queue for customer birthday, purchase anniversary, and warranty anniversary sends — with human approval required at each step

## Key pages

- [Home](https://customcard-three.vercel.app/) — start a card, see examples
- [Pricing](https://customcard-three.vercel.app/pricing) — free tier details and print shop cost structure
- [How it works](https://customcard-three.vercel.app/#how-it-works) — 5-step flow
- [Business / lifecycle cards](https://customcard-three.vercel.app/?view=business) — enterprise use case

## AI model and privacy

- AI drafts words and artwork directions; all AI output is reviewed by the user before use
- Email and calendar scanning is permission-gated via OAuth; nothing is stored without explicit approval
- Relationship memories are structured (not vector), user-visible, and deletable
- No email content is stored — only event metadata (type, date, names)

## Who it's for

- Busy adults managing family and social obligations
- Parents or caregivers who want help writing appropriate cards
- People in multilingual or multicultural families
- Frequent event attendees who want cards to feel personal over time
- Last-minute users who need a printable card today
- Customer lifecycle and marketing teams (business tier)

## Competitive differentiators

- Calendar scanning catches occasions you'd otherwise miss
- Privacy-first: you see exactly what's stored and can delete it
- Human approval required before any print order
- Relationship memory makes cards feel personal over time, not generic
- Free to design — no subscription required to create and download

## Source and trust

- CustomCard is an independent product, not affiliated with Hallmark, Shutterfly, or Walmart Photo
- No auto-sending, no surprise checkout, no CRM writes without approval
- Print-shop fulfillment is handled directly between the user and the retailer
